kind: MECHANICAL HARNESS PREPARATION — two bounded run-local changes, offline only

scopeHonesty.note: No browser was opened and no capture was taken. Nothing in this report is evidence about the game, the renderer, the preview at 127.0.0.1:45091, or any chapter outcome.

changes.title: Pre-capture exact source snapshot + SHA256 manifest in the capture's own folder
changes.what: Before a capture starts (after the output folder is created, before the trace is truncated and before the browser opens), each probe copies byte-exact source of itself, its real local library imports, and the read-only repo probe helpers it imports, into <outDir>/source-snapshot/, with manifest.json holding per-file sha256, repo-relative path and the original absolute path. The manifest hash/ref is bound into summary.json and into a kind:'source-snapshot' trace line.
changes.why: probeSha256 in a summary names bytes that stop existing once the harness is edited again. The snapshot makes a historical probeSha256 reconstructable from the capture itself.
changes.doesNotClaim: Existing captures in verifier/captures/ have no snapshot, were not modified, and are not retroactively described as having this feature.
safety: Only executable source reachable from the probe's own import graph is copied.
Bare/package specifiers and node_modules are recorded as externalSpecifiers, never copied.
No credentials, .env, config secrets or whole-workspace copies; a .env sibling outside the import graph is not read and is covered by test B3.
An existing snapshot manifest in the same folder is a hard error, so an earlier capture directory can never be overwritten or clobbered.
changes.determinism: manifestSha256 covers only the path/sha256/bytes list ordered by path — no timestamps, no absolute paths — so identical bytes give an identical hash and one changed byte changes it.

changes.title: Guaranteed cleanup of the probe-owned browser session on any failure
changes.what: Both probes adopt the session they open into a guard and wrap the measuring body in try/catch/finally. The finally calls guard.stopOnce(), which invokes the session's own stop() at most once. A failure writes failure.json plus a probe-failure trace line and is RE-THROWN unchanged.
changes.why: Both probes previously ended with `await session.stop()` as the last top-level statement, so any throw before it leaked the probe's Chromium. cg-footing-diag hit exactly that at `frameStats(...).catch` (frameStats is synchronous). That TypeError was already corrected before this task; the structural hole is what is now closed for the next failure.
safety: Stops only the session this probe opened; the root-owned preview is never stopped (the probes pass preview:{url, stop(){}} and nothing here reaches past session.stop).
No process killing, no signals, no global browser shutdown.
A cleanup failure is recorded on the guard and logged; it never replaces or hides the original error.
The journey probe's stall FAIL exit code 3 is unchanged: it now sets an exit code and exits AFTER cleanup instead of exiting before it.
changes.outcomeSemanticsPreserved: outcome values, outcomeIsAcceptance:false, stop predicates, checkpoint handling, per-frame/pair provenance, luma visualAcceptance:false, renderer/build/source provenance and the stall predicate are untouched. A crashed capture is PROBE-ERROR-INCONCLUSIVE and never a pass.

all existing captures, snapshots and prior reports

limitations: NO BROWSER OR GAME PROOF. No Chromium, preview, GPU, build, game test or network was used. Sessions in every test are stubs; 'cleanup runs exactly once' means the harness control flow invokes the session's own stop() exactly once, NOT that a real browser process was observed to exit.

The probes' own try/catch/finally blocks are covered by a static structure check (C3) plus behavioural tests of the same helpers they call (A*, D1). They have not been executed against a real capture, because that needs a browser.

The snapshot import walker matches specifiers textually and does not strip comments or strings, so an import-shaped phrase in a comment can add a phantom external entry; the bias is deliberately toward over-recording, never omission. A computed dynamic import is flagged, not resolved.

The snapshot proves which SOURCE ran; it says nothing about the build, the served bundle, the renderer or the outcome. Existing source/build/renderer/per-image provenance is untouched and remains the authority for those.

This feature applies to future captures only. Captures already in verifier/captures/ have no snapshot, were not modified, and their probeSha256 values remain reconstructable only while the referenced harness bytes are unchanged.
Nothing here is chapter verification, acceptance, or a repair of the two blockers in verification-world-interim-report.md; those remain open and unaffected.
